papers.title: Adaptive Multi-head Contrastive Learning
papers.operation: Several projection MLP heads consume features of a common backbone. Pair/head-specific learned temperatures from an additional shared map reweight contrasts and are regularized. The inspected construction retains its given positive/negative relation.
papers.prior_collision: The general ideas of complementary contrastive heads under one backbone and trainable contrast temperatures are already explicit. They cannot be claimed as the GNNM novelty.
papers.bounded_difference: The inspected section does not assign persistent different TRAIN-label-compatible graph-context neighbor targets to internal BE routes or evaluate a retained predictive member ensemble.
papers.limits: Neither full-paper nor code audit; no exact unrestricted absence, novel principle, accuracy guarantee, published-version or result claim.

papers.title: Collaborative Graph Contrastive Learning: Data Augmentation Composition May Not be Necessary for Graph Representation Learning
papers.operation: For a given unchanged graph and X, node representations of one GNN serve as queries and another GNN as keys. Same-node correspondence supplies cross-encoder positives; other nodes are denominator candidates. Each encoder sums peer contrastive losses.
papers.prior_collision: Multiple GNN views and contrastive learning without perturbing the input graph are already explicit. Those broad properties cannot be the GNNM novelty.
papers.bounded_difference: The inspected node operation does not give each private route a fixed different same-class graph-context positive-neighbor relation. It encourages peer same-node agreement. Its displayed operation does not specify the internal BE shared/private parameterization.
papers.limits: No claim of fully independent or tied native parameters from this scope; no architecture/code audit, full-paper or proof audit, published-version or numerical adoption.
